EspoCRM before 10.0.7 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Import scope access to read other users' attachments by supplying a foreign attachmentId to the Import endpoint. Attackers can create an Import record referencing a known attachment ID, then call the error export endpoint to copy source rows into a downloadable CSV they own.

EspoCRM 4.0.0 before 10.0.7 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read restricted emailAddress values via the address-book search API. Users with record access can query address-book search to obtain email addresses even when Roles restrict the emailAddress field.

EspoCRM 4.0.0 before 10.0.7 contains an access control vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read audited field values restricted by field-level security by fetching individual stream notes. Users with stream access to a parent record can request GET /Note/{id}, which skips the NoteAccessControl filter, and recover data.attributes.was and became values of restricted fields.

EspoCRM before 10.0.6 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject HTML by submitting crafted Lead Capture public form data. The request body is stored in LeadCaptureLogRecord.data and rendered unescaped when administrators view the log record, though Content Security Policy blocks JavaScript execution.

EspoCRM before 10.0.6 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that accepts a login stopped at the second factor on routes not requiring authentication. Attackers knowing a 2FA-enabled user's username and password can skip the second factor to read config parameters not exposed publicly.
